subject: Umbrella volume discounts & cross-region consumption — proposed framework
messages:
From: Emma Lin <emma@helixlabs.ai>
To: soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@helixlabs.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — cross-region usage question

Hi Soojin,

Quick one from our procurement/pricing review — we're trying to map expected monthly spend for our global chatbot rollout (US + EU + APAC). Two quick asks:

1) Does Redwood allow a single committed volume (monthly token commit) to be consumed across regions with a single blended per-token rate, or do you require region-specific commit buckets?
2) If umbrella commits are allowed, how do you handle APAC surcharge / egress or region-specific minimums? Also: any standard language on rollover credits if monthly commit isn't used?

I've attached a short PDF with our projected region splits and a sample month. Can you point us to a concise pricing example (blended rate calculation) we can show finance?

Thanks —
Emma Lin
Head of Product
Helix Labs

Attachment: Helix_Pricing_Questions.pdf (1 page)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — cross-region usage question

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear note and the sample month. High-level answers first, then a short proposal below.

Short answers:
- Umbrella commits: Yes — we can support a single committed token pool for Hosted API that spans regions. That pool is billed at a blended per-token rate based on the commit tier you sign up for.
- APAC handling: We typically apply a small APAC surcharge (0.5–1.5% or a fixed $/token delta depending on model family) to cover regional capacity and egress variability for sustained heavy usage. If you need strict regional separation for compliance, we can carve an APAC-only bucket.
- Rollover: We offer limited rollover credits (up to 20% of monthly commit) for 60 days for enterprise contracts; can be expanded with a higher commitment.

Proposal (attached spreadsheet with worked examples):
- Option A (Umbrella commit): Single monthly commit (e.g., 10B tokens) across US/EU/APAC. Blended rate = tier price adjusted by region weight + APAC surcharge applied only to APAC consumption for bookkeeping.
- Option B (Regional buckets): Commit split by region (e.g., 6B US / 3B EU / 1B APAC) at region-specific tier prices — provides clearer SLAs per-region.

Next steps I suggest: Dylan (cc'd) will draft a worked blended example with your sample month and show the effective per-token price for both A and B, plus impact of a 12‑month vs 24‑month commit. Marissa can outline SOW/operational items if you prefer Option A.

I'll attach a simple pricing model XLSX — feel free to mark it up.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Proposed_Pricing_Model.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Emma Lin <emma@helixlabs.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — cross-region usage question

Emma / Soojin — I populated the spreadsheet with three commit scenarios and the blended math. Key points from the model:

- Tier breakpoints (example): 0-1B, 1B-5B, 5B-20B. Per-token list prices decrease by ~20–30% between brackets.
- Blended rate calculation: (US_tokens * US_rate + EU_tokens * EU_rate + APAC_tokens * (APAC_rate + surcharge)) / total_tokens_consumed. If umbrella commit, you use the committed tier price for the total tokens to pick the base rate, then apply small APAC delta on consumption for reporting.
- Example (from your sample month): total = 1.2B tokens (US 65%, EU 28%, APAC 7%). If you take a 5B-month commit, effective blended rate = $0.0009/token (US/EU) and APAC effective = $0.000915/token after 1% APAC uplift. Net blended for the month = $0.000901/token.
- Rollover rules implemented in sheet: up to 20% rollover, credits expire after 60 days. Option to negotiate larger rollover windows for multi-year deals.

I've also added a short clause you can show procurement on how we allocate unused tokens and the monthly reconciliation process.

Attachment: Proposed_Pricing_Model.xlsx (updated)

From: Emma Lin <emma@helixlabs.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@helixlabs.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — cross-region usage question

Thanks Dylan — that helps a lot. A couple follow-ups from procurement and finance:

1) Can you provide a worked example that includes token overage pricing if we exceed the monthly commit by ~15%? Procurement wants to see the marginal cost step.
2) For compliance we need confirmation about data residency for EU traffic — will routing EU traffic to EU endpoints be mandatory for the blended model, or can we route cross-region depending on capacity?
3) Any change to SLA if we consume from umbrella pool vs region buckets?

Also, can you send a short SOW stub so our legal team can start reviewing operational terms (data retention, logs, support hours)?

Best —
Emma

Attachment: none

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Lin <emma@helixlabs.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, logan.wright@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — cross-region usage question

Emma — great questions. Short answers here and attachments for legal/finance.

1) Overage pricing: We charge a stepped overage at the next consumption bracket rate. In the example sheet I added a marginal cost row: exceeding commit by 15% for your sample month would increase effective per-token cost by ~12–18% depending on model family. I added a worked numeric example in the "overage_examples" tab.

2) Data residency & routing: For umbrella commits we support "preferred-region routing" — EU-origin traffic will be routed to EU endpoints by default to satisfy residency. We do allow cross-region routing for burst scenarios with your consent (we log and show region of execution in Console). If you require strict EU-only execution, we recommend a regional bucket to enforce it.

3) SLA: No SLA change for umbrella vs regional buckets; SLA is at the tenant level. However, regional buckets can have tighter per-region capacity commitments (reserved APAC capacity) as an add-on.

Attachments included: a short SOW stub (Novus_SOW_v2.pdf) with operational items, plus the updated pricing model. If this looks good, I'd propose a 12-month umbrella commit at the 5B tier with optional APAC reserved pocket (1B) to reduce the APAC surcharge.

Next steps:
- Emma / Procurement: confirm appetite for 12-month umbrella commit + optional APAC pocket.
- Marissa: I looped you for SOW and Ops onboarding checklist.

Thanks —
Soojin Lee
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Novus_SOW_v2.pdf, Proposed_Pricing_Model.xlsx
